issues.description: Same nil-guard boilerplate copy-pasted into ~20 accessors instead of pushed into one helper or the data structure
issues.detail: Every getter now opens with `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(x, ...)`. A single helper (e.g. `sliceOrNil(f, func(*File)[]T)`) or making the receiving types nil-tolerant would collapse each accessor to one line and state the 'nil receiver yields empty' invariant once. The panics were removed by adding a special case everywhere instead of removing the special case.

issues.description: Reflection-driven zero test is too clever and silently skips methods that take arguments or expose Len()
issues.detail: testZeroAny walks NumMethod, filters to NumIn==1, and name-special-cases IsZero/ValueNodeIndex/Context. Accessors with parameters are never exercised, and any return type with a Len() int method passes the heuristic regardless of semantics. A boring explicit table of (name, func(T) any) cases would be longer but durable; at minimum add an allowlist so new accessors cannot silently escape coverage.

issues.description: Imports.Transitive/Directs closures capture i and rely on empty-slice guard instead of bailing out on nil
issues.detail: When i==nil the slice is empty so the Indexer body never runs, but the mapper closures still capture i and dereference i.publicEnd / i.importEnd. The next refactor that drops the length guard will crash. Bail out early returning an empty Indexer when i==nil, or assert non-nil at the top, and document the 'last element is implicit descriptor.proto' invariant that Transitive's max(0,len-1) depends on.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex sentinel -1 on zero is inconsistent with the rest of the zero-value convention
issues.detail: Every other zero accessor returns the zero value of its return type; ValueNodeIndex returns -1, forcing callers to know two sentinels and the test to hard-code a name-based exception. Either encode the optionality in the type (an Index with Ok(), or (int, bool)) or return 0 and require IsZero checks. Pick one convention.

issues.description: Test mixed with ~20 behavioral nil-guard fixes in one commit makes future bisect useless
issues.detail: The change is at least two patches: add the zero-sweep test (red), then land each panic fix as its own diff. As submitted, a bisect on any future regression in File.Imports or similar accessors lands on 'add zero test', which is not the actual change. Split the commit.

issues.description: Two nil-zero idioms (`f == nil` vs `IsZero()`) coexist in the same package
issues.detail: *File methods guard with `f == nil`; value types like Type, Member, Oneof guard with `!t.IsZero()`. Both are reasonable but mixing them forces every maintainer to remember which type uses which convention. Pick one (e.g. always IsZero, with *File.IsZero defined as `f == nil`) so the rule is stated once.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the change is directionally correct and the new zero-value reflection test is a valuable structural check, but the implementation needs cleanup before landing. The dominant complaint (all three reviewers) is that the same nil-guard boilerplate was copy-pasted into ~20 accessors instead of pushed into one helper or the receiving types. The reflection test itself is too clever — it silently skips methods with arguments and trusts any Len() method as a length probe. Imports.Transitive/Directs rely on an empty-slice guard while their closures still capture and dereference the nil receiver, which is fragile. Verdict: needs-work — split the commit, unify the nil idiom behind one helper, and tighten the test from reflection-discovery to an explicit table.
